This matter is taken up through Hybrid arrangement (video conferencing/physical mode).
Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned counsel for the State.

This is an application under section 483 of B.N.S.S. read with section 439 of Cr.P.C. in connection with G.R. Case No.691 of 2024 arising out of Kabisuryanagar P.S. Case No.703 of 2024 pending in the Court of learned J.M.F.C., Kabisuryanagar for offences punishable under sections 328/376(2)(n)/341/323/294/506/34 of the Indian Penal Code read with section 67(A) of the Information Technology Act, 2000.
The prayer for bail of the petitioner was rejected by the learned Additional Sessions Judge, Kodala vide order dated 19.03.2025.
Considering the submission made by the learned counsel for the petitioner that the petitioner is in judicial custody since 03.11.2024 and charge sheet has been submitted under sections 328/376(2)(n)/341/323/294/ 506/34 of the Indian Penal Code read with section 67(A) of the Information Technology Act, 2000 and after going through the 164 Cr.P.C. statement of the victim,
Dhiraj Kumar Nayak @ vs State Of Odisha .... Opp. Party on 9 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/128461952/
1 who is aged about nineteen years, produced by the learned counsel for the petitioner, which is taken on record and the materials available on record and after hearing the learned counsel for the State, I am inclined to release the petitioner on bail.
Let the petitioner be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a bail bond of Rs.50,000/-
(rupees fifty thousand) with two local solvent sureties each for the like amount to the satisfaction of the learned Court in seisin over the matter with further conditions as the learned Court may deem just and proper subject to conditions that the petitioner shall appear before the learned trial Court on each date to which the case would be posted for trial and shall not try to come in contact with the victim.
Violation of any terms and conditions shall entail cancellation of bail.
